trace.question: Can we send a promotional text at 10pm?
trace.answer:
No. Our Customer Messaging Policy doesn't allow it. [Customer Messaging Policy §3, Quiet Hours] bans texts of any kind between 8pm and 9am in the customer's local time. If we don't know a customer's local time, we use Central time. A 10pm send would fall inside that window.

Promotional texts can go out between 9am and 8pm in the customer's local time. They also have to meet the other messaging rules:
- **Consent:** The customer must have verified SMS consent, and anyone who has unsubscribed is excluded [Customer Messaging Policy §2, Who May Receive Marketing Texts].
- **Frequency:** No customer gets more than four marketing texts in a calendar month [Customer Messaging Policy §4, Frequency].
- **Offers:** A discount can't exceed 15% or $10, whichever is lower, unless you approve it. The offer needs an expiry date within 14 days and the words "one per customer" [Customer Messaging Policy §5, Offers in Messages].

I can't schedule or send texts myself. I can propose a campaign for you to approve, timed within the allowed hours.

case.question: A customer wants to cancel a catering order three days before pickup. Do they get the deposit back?

trace.question: A customer wants to cancel a catering order three days before pickup. Do they get the deposit back?
trace.answer:
Yes. Cancelling three days (72 hours) before pickup is before the 48-hour cutoff, so the customer gets the deposit back. The policy says the deposit is refundable up to 48 hours before pickup and kept after that [House Policy §6, Catering].

The deadline is the pickup time minus 48 hours. That gives the customer about one more day to cancel and still get the refund. If the order is over $300, the policy says the owner has to confirm catering orders of that size. It doesn't say whether that also applies to a cancellation. I didn't look up a specific order, so I haven't checked its total or pickup time.

Yes. The student can have both. House policy says a free loyalty drink is not a discount, so it can be combined with a standard discount on the rest of the order. The student discount is 10% with a valid student ID [House Policy §4, Discounts].

Also check that the reward is still valid. A free drink reward expires 60 days after it was issued [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program].

case.question: Can a lead give a regular 25% off a catering order?

trace.question: Can a lead give a regular 25% off a catering order?
trace.answer:
Yes on the lead's authority, with two catch-alls. A 25% discount is above 20%, so a lead can't give it alone. [House Policy §4, Discounts] says any discount above 10% needs a lead, and any discount above 20% needs the owner (Dana). A regular customer isn't one of the standard discount groups, which are students, hospital staff, and the loyalty reward. So the discount would fall under the "other discount" rule, and the owner has to approve 25%.

Catering has its own rule. Orders over $300 need the owner's confirmation, and catering needs 72 hours' notice and a 50% deposit [House Policy §6, Catering]. Seasonal Specials can't be discounted at all, so they would have to come off the discounted amount.

A lead could give up to 20% on their own authority. Anything higher needs Dana's approval first.

trace.question: How many stamps earn a free drink, and can it be used on a Seasonal Special?
trace.answer:
Nine stamps earn a free drink. You earn one stamp per drink when you give your phone number at checkout. [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program]

The free drink can't be used on a Seasonal Special. That section excludes Seasonal Specials, Flights, and Bubble Tea. The reward covers any size from Signature Drinks, House Favorites, or Matcha. [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program]

Seasonal Specials are also never discounted. [House Policy §4, Discounts]

A free drink reward expires 60 days after it is issued. Stamps expire 12 months after they are earned. [Online Ordering and Loyalty Policy §4, Loyalty Program]
